headline: High risk of capability conflict and cascading error: Plane can write files and Unstructured can read/write and execute subprocesses, creating unsafe shared-workspace workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane exposes file uploads and broad network egress, while Unstructured reads files and processes documents in a partitioned pipeline. If Plane-supplied content is placed into a shared workspace, Unstructured may parse attacker-controlled text as data. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Plane uploads are copied into a shared directory that Unstructured reads
IF Unstructured treats document text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Store uploads in separate directories per agent
Strip instruction-like text before handing files to Unstructured
Require explicit human review of extracted text before reuse
Use read-only mounts for Unstructured inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every file handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, and can make broad network egress; Unstructured reads files and writes outputs in a container. A shared workspace could expose Plane-managed content to Unstructured processing, creating leakage of sensitive work products. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so medium is the safest supported choice.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or mounted volume
IF Plane-managed files include sensitive issues, notes, or roadmaps
mitigations: Separate workspaces by agent
Limit Unstructured input folders to non-sensitive documents
Disable unnecessary network egress during processing
Review output files before syncing back to Plane
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plane does not write its own filesystem, but Unstructured can read and write files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. In a shared directory or orchestrated pipeline, Unstructured can overwrite or transform artifacts that Plane later consumes, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination. Because the write surface is real and defaults are not isolated, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Plane consumes artifacts that Unstructured may rewrite or replace
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Make Plane inputs read-only to Unstructured
Run Unstructured in a separate container volume
Serialize handoffs with a manual approval step
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can surface files and notes, and Unstructured is a document-processing system that can emit extracted text for downstream use. If Plane output is fed into Unstructured and then reused by Plane or another workflow without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect tasks or records. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF Unstructured output is imported back into Plane without review
IF extracted text is treated as authoritative task or issue content
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text
Keep source documents attached to derived records
Compare extracted fields against originals for critical items
Mark machine-generated fields clearly in Plane
requires-engineering: add validation rules for downstream imports

E_compliance.rationale: Plane lists privacy/security contact surfaces and self-hosted deployment, while Unstructured exposes a privacy-policy endpoint and runs in a Docker container. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance concern is supported. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair's combined handling of the same data classes.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through both agents under different retention or residency policies
IF the deployment mixes self-hosted Plane data with externally governed Unstructured processing
mitigations: Review both privacy policies before deployment
Keep regulated data out of the shared pipeline
Document retention settings for each agent
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated data
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls
